ledger.note: July 1540: the Mughals abandon the Punjab. Sher Shah Suri page: 'As Humayun reached Lahore in July 1540, the Afghans were at Sultanpur Lodhi. With the approach of the Afghans, the Mughals fled Lahore'; Sher Shah 'advanced from Sirhind toward Lahore, and then continued toward the Chenab river before arriving at Khushab', received the submission of the Baloch chiefs between the Chenab and the Indus, and 'stationed 50,000 men in Punjab'. At Khushab 'Humayun and Kamran quarreled and parted ways, with Humayun leaving for Sindh, and Kamran to Kabul'. Humayun page: Kamran offered Sher Shah to revolt 'in return for most of the Punjab'. Humayun holds no land from here until Kandahar (October 1545) and Kabul (November 1545). Cliopatria keeps the Punjab Mughal to 1546 and its Sur row takes it only in 1547: the sur-empire dossier should carry the Punjab from July 1540.

wars.name: Mughal-Afghan Wars

zones.text: the Punjab and Hindustan, the ground of the Afghan-Mughal struggle

wars.outcome: From Panipat (21 April 1526) to 3 April 1752: the Lodi fall, the Sur Interregnum of 1540-1555 and Humayun's return, and the Durrani take of the Punjab; the infobox closes the wars on 3 April 1752.
wars.note: One umbrella entry from the main page's infobox; the individual campaigns follow.

wars.name: Battle of Khanwa
wars.outcome: Mughal victory: Babur's forces defeated Rana Sanga's Rajput armies near Agra, 'a year later' than Panipat. No territory is dated on the page.
wars.note: The year is inferred from 'a year later' than 1526.

wars.name: Humayun's Gujarat campaign
wars.outcome: Humayun took Mandu and Champaner within a month in 1535; 'Bahadur Shah recaptured all of Gujarat in 1536 and began an attack on Malwa'. Bahadur Shah, escaping, 'took up refuge with the Portuguese' (page).

wars.name: Sher Shah's war on Humayun (Chausa and Kannauj)

zones.text: the Ganges plain from Chausa to Kannauj

wars.outcome: Sher Shah won at Chausa (June 1539) and at Kannauj (17 May 1540); Humayun fled into fifteen years of exile and the Mughal Interregnum began.
wars.note: The Sur Empire is Sher Shah's state; Cliopatria's Sur row begins in 1540.

wars.name: Humayun's reconquest of Hindustan
wars.outcome: Sikandar Shah Suri was defeated at Sirhind on 22 June 1555 and Humayun sat on the throne at Delhi on 23 July 1555.

wars.name: Second Battle of Panipat
wars.outcome: Bairam Khan defeated Hemu and the Sur army on 5 November 1556, securing Delhi-Agra for Akbar.

wars.name: Conquest of Malwa
wars.outcome: Baz Bahadur was beaten at Sarangpur in 1560; the Mughals annexed Malwa the following year.

wars.name: Mughal invasion of Marwar
wars.outcome: A twenty-year invasion (infobox span); Marwar returned as a Mughal-allied state; the page gives no dated sieges.

wars.name: Conquest of Garha
wars.outcome: Rani Durgavati was defeated at the Battle of Damoh and 'committed suicide'; Garha fell to the Mughals.

wars.name: Siege of Chittorgarh (1567-1568)
wars.outcome: 'Chittorgarh fell in February 1568 after a siege of four months'; Ranthambore followed in 1568.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Gujarat
wars.outcome: Akbar occupied Ahmedabad in 1572 and won a decisive victory on 2 September 1573.

wars.name: Battle of Haldighati
wars.outcome: Mewar 'was later defeated by the Mughals at the Battle of Haldighati in 1576'; no territorial result is on the page.
wars.note: The Mewar dossier records the hill country as occupied 1576-1585.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Bengal

union.text: Patna and Bihar

wars.outcome: Patna was seized from Daud Khan in 1574, the Mughals won at Tukaroi in 1575 and Rajmahal (1576) ended the war; Orissa stayed a Karrani fief.
wars.note: Daud Khan Karrani's sultanate is drawn under Cliopatria's Sur Empire row.

wars.name: Akbar's conquest of Kabul
wars.outcome: 'In August 1581, Akbar seized Kabul'; it became a province in 1585.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Kashmir
wars.outcome: An army was sent in 1585; Yaqub surrendered to Akbar at Srinagar in June 1589.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Sindh
wars.outcome: 'Jani Beg surrendered to the Mughals in 1591'.

wars.name: Akbar's Deccan campaigns

union.text: Berar

wars.outcome: Operations began in 1593; Berar was ceded in 1595, Ahmadnagar fort taken in August 1600 and Asirgarh on 17 January 1601; Prince Daniyal governed the new subahs.

wars.name: Mughal-Safavid War (1622-1623)
wars.outcome: The Safavids took Kandahar on 22 June after a 45-day siege; the Mughals recovered it only in 1638.
wars.note: The page's surrounding text hints at 1621; the war is labelled 1622-1623.

wars.name: Shah Jahan's Deccan campaigns
wars.outcome: Daulatabad was captured in 1632 (1633 in a linked title) and the Nizam Shahi king imprisoned; 'Golconda submitted in 1635 and then Bijapur in 1636'.

wars.name: Fall of Kandahar (1638)
wars.outcome: Ali Mardan Khan handed Kandahar over to Shah Jahan; it stayed Mughal until 1649.

wars.name: Shah Jahan's Balkh and Badakhshan campaign
wars.outcome: 'They retreated from the fruitless lands, and Balkh and Badakhshan returned to Bukharan control'; Balkh was relinquished in 1647.

wars.name: Mughal-Safavid war (1649-1653)
wars.outcome: Safavid victory: Kandahar taken on 22 February 1649, Mughal sieges of 1649, 1651, 1652 and 1653 all failed (given up 29 September 1653).
wars.note: The Khan of Bukhara sent 10,000 troops toward Kabul in May 1652 as the Safavids' ally.

wars.name: Mughal-Maratha Wars

wars.name: Nader Shah's invasion of India

wars.name: Battle of Buxar

wars.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War

wars.note: The Mughal emperor was the prize, not a combatant.

wars.name: Indian Rebellion of 1857

zones.text: Delhi city and the territory as far as Palam

wars.outcome: The sepoys proclaimed Bahadur Shah II at Delhi; the Siege of Delhi ended on 21 September 1857, Zafar was captured on 20 September, tried in 1858 and exiled to Rangoon on 7 October 1858.

wars.name: Ahom-Mughal conflicts

zones.text: Kamrup between the Barnadi and the Manas

wars.outcome: The Mughals take western Assam by the Treaty of Asurar Ali (February 1639), lose Guwahati in 1658, retake it with Mir Jumla's invasion of 1662 (Ghilajharighat, January 1663), lose it on 2 November 1667, are handed it again in March 1679 and are driven back to the Manas at Itakhuli in 1682, which becomes the boundary.
wars.note: Same war and zones as the ahom-kingdom dossier (Ahom-Mughal wars), added by the review fix.

wars.name: Siege of Bijapur (1685-1686)

zones.text: Bijapur fort and the country round it

wars.name: Rathore rebellion in Marwar

notes:
Phase B dossier for the Mughal Empire, group sa-05-a. Page budget: 14 pages opened (Mughal Empire, Humayun, Akbar, Aurangzeb, Mughal-Persian wars, Mughal-Safavid war 1649-1653, Shah Jahan, Nader Shah's invasion of India, Mughal successor states, Maratha Empire, Durrani Empire, Shah Alam II, Bahadur Shah Zafar, Mughal-Maratha Wars); Shah Alam II was read twice (same page).

CLIOPATRIA ROWS TO FIX (start of the review): (1) The Mughal row starts in 1529 but the empire began on 21 April 1526; 1526-1528 are Cliopatria's Timurid row (Babur's Kabul-Kandahar-Punjab) plus Lodi row (the Delhi core): new keyframe mughal-empire_1526 is their union and the Timurid and Lodi dossiers should end in 1526. (2) The 1783-1856 shapes (0.24-0.36 M km2, about 70 per cent Rajasthan) are not what the emperor ruled: Shah Alam II page 'was only left with Delhi city to rule' (1783), Bahadur Shah Zafar page 'reduced to only the city of Delhi and the surrounding territory as far as Palam'; verdict wrong, correction = Cliopatria's own 1857 Delhi shape (578 km2). The 1811-1856 shape also overlaps the British Empire rows. (3) Kandahar: the shapes lose its western half only in 1626 (page: 1622), regain it in 1640 (page: 1638) and lose it again in 1648 (page: 22 February 1649); the keyframes 1612, 1626, 1640, 1648 are adjusted by year. (4) Bengal 1576 (not 1579), Sindh 1591 (not 1595), Malwa 1561 (not 1564), Awadh 1722 and Hyderabad 1724 (Cliopatria 1727), Malwa lost 1738 (Cliopatria 1741): new keyframes 1561, 1576, 1591, 1722, 1724 and adjusted 1738/1741. (5) The 1741 shape lacks Lahore and Multan although the Nader page has the lands east of the Indus handed back (Cliopatria's 1744 shape has them). (6) Seed bboxes of several shapes reach lon 63.8 (1713, 1748, ...) but no cell lies west of 65.5 E: a bbox artefact, not a shape problem.

NOT VERIFIED (page budget, verdict ok with 'unverified' notes): Babur's conquests 1527-1529 and the eastern edge in 1529; who held the Punjab in 1540-46 (Kamran or the Sur); Kabul under Muhammad Hakim 1556-1581; the Jahangir years (1605-1627: no page opened; the shapes 1600/1612 differ by a Bengal-east edge only); Shah Jahan's Assam/Kamrup gain 1639 and loss 1648 (the Ahom dossier has them); the 1653, 1659, 1662, 1673, 1677, 1734 steps; the Carnatic part of the 1691 shape; the 1741-1744 drop of 1.1 M km2 (Gujarat, Bundelkhand, Orissa, Kashmir, Berar, Khandesh); the 1772-1782 extent. PROTECTORATE OF THE EMPEROR (recorded by the protectors, not here): the Marathas protected the emperor from January 1772 and officially from 1784 ('in 1784 the Marathas officially became the protectors of the emperor in Delhi'), the British from 14 September 1803 to 1857; the Maratha and British dossiers should carry the vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart mughal-empire.
